rows.R: Main p1 abstract and p3 Results give HbA1c changes as unsigned 0.2% and 1.6% with signed CIs (-0.5 to 0.2; -1.8 to -1.3); +1.6 lies outside its CI. Table 2 p6 (rendered) prints -0.2 and -1.6 with the same CIs, so the intended signed values are recoverable. Sign presentation error, not a numerical error.
rows.evidence: jama_courcoulas...pdf p1, p3 (text), p6 Table 2 (rendered 220 dpi); card C001 read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Abstract: 'HbA1c decreased by 0.2% (95% CI, -0.5% to 0.2%)... by 1.6% (95% CI, -1.8% to -1.3%)'. p3: 'difference, 0.2% [95% CI, -0.5% to 0.2%]' and 'difference, 1.6% [95% CI, -1.8% to -1.3%]'. Table 2: -0.2 (-0.5 to 0.2), -1.6 (-1.8 to -1.3); footnote b: net change for HbA1c. The prose mixes a decrease magnitude with a signed interval; 1.6 is outside [-1.8,-1.3]. Baseline/year-7 means (8.7 to 7.2; 8.2 to 8.0) confirm direction. The reader can recover the signed estimate from Table 2, so the issue is confirmed but presentational. Card agrees; did not change my view.

rows.R: Year-12 HbA1c difference -1.1 (95% CI -1.7 to -0.5) has P=.002 in main p1/p3 but P<.001 in eTable 2 (supp2 p15). CI-implied P (Wald) = 0.00033; over all rounding-consistent limits with estimate at the midpoint, max P = 0.0009, so .002 is incompatible with the printed CI. Both significant; interpretation unchanged.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p3 (text); supp2 p4-5 methods, p15 eTable 2 (text); card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: Same contrast, same interval in both places. R: p_from_ci(-1.1,-1.7,-0.5,ratio=FALSE)=0.000327; with limits in [-1.75,-1.65] and [-0.55,-0.45] and estimate at the midpoint, P ranges 0.00009 to 0.00091. A t reference with large df does not move this materially. eTable 2's <.001 agrees with the interval; main text's .002 does not. The July 2024 correction concerns only the registry link. Confirmed reporting inconsistency; the P value is rarely an extraction input and both values are below .05, so minor.

rows.R: Abstract p1: '4 deaths (2.2%), 2 in each group' among 262 enrolled. 4/262 = 1.53%; Table 3 p8 gives 2/96 (2.1%) and 2/166 (1.2%), both correct. No denominator in the paper yields 2.2% for 4 deaths. The abstract percentage overstates pooled mortality.
rows.evidence: Main p1 abstract, p3 cohort, p4 Table 1 headers, p7 death narrative, p8 Table 3 (text); card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: R: 100*4/262 = 1.527; 2/96 = 2.083; 2/166 = 1.205. 2.2% would require a denominator near 182. Possibly an averaging or copying slip (e.g., 2.1 rounded up) but no source explains it. Mortality is a headline safety result in the abstract and a percentage could be extracted directly; counts are clear, so the error is recoverable, but I rate it substantive because the abstract figure is wrong by ~0.7 percentage points (relative ~44%).

rows.R: Plan (supp1 p17, p26-27, p29 Table A1, Fig A1) defines the primary outcome as relative percent change in HbA1c (power: -15% vs -7% to +2%). Report Table 2 footnote b and eTable 2 present net (absolute) change for HbA1c (-1.4 points), while main p2 still says 'percent change'. The reported primary scale differs from the planned one.
rows.evidence: Supp1 (protocol v6) p17, p26-29; main p2-3, p6 Table 2 (rendered); supp2 p4, p15-16 (text).
rows.rationale: Plan model A1: Y = percent change of HbA1c; beta7 = difference in mean percent changes; power simulations on the relative scale. Report: Table 2 footnote b 'Net change presented for HbA1c', values -0.2/-1.6/-1.4 equal to absolute differences in HbA1c % units (8.7 to 7.2 = -1.5 points; a relative change would be about -17%). The report's methods text calls the outcome 'percent change', which is ambiguous between HbA1c units and relative change, creating an additional internal ambiguity. The analysis scale actually reported is net change; this is a primary-outcome scale difference from the plan, not disclosed.

rows.R: Plan supp1 p18 and p29 Table A1 define remission as HbA1c <6.5% without diabetes medications, no duration; main p2 adds 'for at least 3 months, assessed annually'. Difference exists, but the plan defers operational definitions to a Manual of Operations (p18) that was not supplied, so whether the 3-month window is new cannot be settled.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p18, p29; main p1-2, p6 Table 2, p7 Figure 3 caption (text).
rows.rationale: Threshold and medication criteria agree; only the explicit >=3-month medication-free requirement is added in the report. Figure 3 caption repeats the plan wording without a duration. Because protocol section 4.4 says detailed definitions and algorithms are in the Manual of Operations, the added window may be an operational specification rather than a change. Retained as a documented definitional difference; L indeterminate.

rows.R: Plan Table A1 (supp1 p30) lists 'major adverse cardiovascular events' under Aim 2 Safety; main p2 lists MACE among secondary outcomes. However, plan section 4.3 (p18) already lists 'microvascular or macrovascular events' as secondary and p18 says some study outcomes are also secondary, so the status change is mainly a labeling difference.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p18, p29-30, p34; main p1-2, p8 Table 3 (text).
rows.rationale: Plan secondary list includes macrovascular events (operationally only stroke named) and the safety list includes MACE; report groups MACE with secondary outcomes and analyzes it descriptively in Table 3 without a composite. The hierarchy label differs, but the plan's own secondary 'macrovascular events' category overlaps MACE. A real but small labeling difference; minor_presentation.

rows.R: Plan model A1 (supp1 p26) has group, visit, group x visit and site (Z = site indicators) as fixed effects; baseline HbA1c appears only among further sensitivity covariates (p34). Report primary model (main p2-3; supp2 p4) adds baseline HbA1c as a fixed effect. Covariate set of the primary model changed; not disclosed as a change.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p26-27, p34; main p2-3; supp2 p4 (text).
rows.rationale: Adding baseline HbA1c to a change-from-baseline model (ANCOVA-type adjustment) changes the estimator and usually its precision; it is a change to the prespecified primary analysis. The plan's sensitivity list includes baseline HbA1c, so the reported primary resembles a planned sensitivity model; neither report location calls this a change.

rows.R: Plan supp1 p30-31, p34 promises MICE with Rubin's rules, pattern-mixture models, a censoring weight combined with IPTW, a per-protocol analysis discarding post-crossover outcomes, and baseline-covariate sensitivity analyses. Searched main and supp2 in full: only the treatment-IPW per-protocol analysis (main p3, supp2 p5, eFigure 2) is reported; no MICE, pattern-mixture or discard analysis.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p30-31, p34; main p3, p9; supp2 p4-6 and contents list (text search for imput/pattern/Rubin/discard/sensitivity).
rows.rationale: Text search of supp2 and main for 'imput', 'pattern', 'Rubin', 'discard', 'censoring weight' found none of these analyses. The report's IPW weight (supp2 p5) contains only treatment-history terms. MAR is asserted instead (main p3, supp2 p5-6; limitation p9). Planned sensitivity analyses of the primary outcome were not reported; retained as a plan-report difference.

rows.R: Plan supp1 p27 specifies mixed-effects logistic models (A2, patient random intercept; conditional log OR) for glycemic control and remission; report (main p3; supp2 p4) uses GEE with sandwich SEs adjusting for site and baseline HbA1c. Model family and estimand (conditional vs marginal OR) differ; baseline HbA1c covariate also added.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p27; main p3, p6 Table 2; supp2 p4-5, p15 eTable 2 (text).
rows.rationale: A GLMM yields subject-specific ORs, GEE population-averaged ORs; these are different estimands and are not interchangeable for extraction. No A2 results reported. Change not described as a deviation.

rows.R: Table 2 p6 (rendered) medical 'use of medications' OR 0.10 (0.01 to 3.27): geometric midpoint sqrt(0.01*3.27)=0.18; with 0.01 in [0.005,0.015] the midpoint range is 0.128-0.222, excluding 0.10. All 17 other binary OR cells reproduce (ratio 0.98-1.06; 0.03 (0.01-0.11) fits within rounding). Lower limit implied by 0.10 and 3.27 is 0.003, so the lower bound is likely misprinted.
rows.evidence: Main p6 Table 2 (rendered 220 dpi); supp2 p4 GEE method, p15 eTable 2 for comparison (text); card read after judgment.
rows.rationale: R: geometric midpoints computed for all 18 binary cells; only this cell fails (ratio 0.553). Implied lower limit 0.10^2/3.27 = 0.0031 (range 0.0028-0.0034 for estimate 0.095-0.105). The year-12 analogue in eTable 2, 0.06 (0.002, 2.16), reproduces (sqrt = 0.066), suggesting a display slip for a limit around 0.003. A within-group year-7/baseline OR in the medical arm is not the group comparison and unlikely to be extracted; confirmed but minor.

rows.R: Plan supp1 p34 specifies Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests for micro/macrovascular events and safety outcomes; report supp2 p6 and eTable 5/6 footnotes use chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Stratified versus unstratified test; the plan does not name the strata. Low-stakes method change for descriptive safety comparisons.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p26, p34-35; supp2 p6, p17, p19-21 footnotes; main p1, p7 (text).
rows.rationale: CMH implies stratification (presumably site); the report applies ordinary chi-squared/Fisher tests. The planned stratified analysis is not reported. Retained as a method difference.

rows.R: Within the plan (supp1): model A1 (p26) treats site as a fixed effect b_i (with Z also site indicators), but the power section (p28) uses a fitted variance component sigma_b=0.06 for site, and p31 says site-specific effects 'follow some distribution' and the CI describes heterogeneity, i.e., a random-site model. Fixed versus random site is internally inconsistent in the plan.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p26-28, p31 (text); report main p2-3, supp2 p4 for context (fixed site used).
rows.rationale: The plan's model equation, power simulation and interpretive paragraph describe incompatible site specifications. This affects how the estimand and the power simulation are understood (average-of-sites random-effects interpretation versus fixed-site adjustment). The reported analysis follows fixed site. Rated substantive because it concerns the primary model specification, not wording.

rows.R: Plan Appendix 2 (supp1 p55-56): randomized 155+69+43+45+43 = 355, underwent intervention 154+61+38+40+32 = 325, so 30 did not start; the dagger footnote says 38 dropped at randomization. Died (3), lost (20) and eligible (302) reconcile with p27. The 38 conflicts with the table. Note: the report (main p3, Fig 1) states 39 withdrew before intervention and 316 eligible, closer to the footnote.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p27, p55-56 (text); main p3 Figure 1 for context.
rows.rationale: Sums computed: 355, 325, difference 30 vs footnote 38; 2+0+0+1+0 = 3 deaths; 12+5+3+0+0 = 20 lost; 140+56+35+39+32 = 302 eligible = 325-20-3. Real plan-internal count inconsistency in background enrollment accounting; it does not alter the planned analysis but affects understanding of pre-intervention exclusions. Rated minor_presentation. The plan-vs-report difference (325 initiated vs 316 eligible) is outside this candidate.

rows.R: eTable 1 (supp2 p14) 7-year column: Other race 4 (1.9) with N=262; 4/262 = 1.5%. Black 81 (30.9) and White 176 (67.2) reproduce, but 81+176+4 = 261. Main Table 1 gives White 59+118 = 177 (67.6%), so eTable 1 White (176) also disagrees with Table 1.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p14 eTable 1 (text); main p4 Table 1 (text).
rows.rationale: R: 4/262 = 1.527%, 81/262 = 30.92%, 176/262 = 67.18%, 177/262 = 67.56%. Main Table 1: Black 35+46 = 81, White 59+118 = 177, Other 2+2 = 4, totals 96 and 166 reconcile. eTable 1 Other percentage wrong and White count one lower than Table 1; abstract 67.2% White matches eTable's 176, not Table 1's 177. Small demographic display errors; minor.

rows.R: Main p4: follow-up imaging was MRI in 8/336 (2%) and CT in 328/336 (98%); main p9 and eTable 11 (supp5 p51): MR diffusion follow-up in 204 (61%) = 101+24+79; discussion p11 'two-thirds'. 8 matches baseline MR DWI (Table 1: 3+5), so p4 appears to describe baseline modality as follow-up. Reader cannot tell which follow-up modality mix applies to infarct volumes.
rows.evidence: Main p4, p5 Table 1, p9, p11 (text); supp5 p51 eTable 11 (text).
rows.rationale: 204/336 = 60.7%; 8/336 = 2.4%; 101+24+79 = 204. The two statements cannot both describe the follow-up imaging population. Table 1 shows 8 patients with baseline MR DWI, a plausible source of the p4 numbers. Follow-up infarct volume and growth analyses depend on the modality (DWI vs CT), so the error bears on interpretation of those post hoc results. Outside this candidate: main p9 gives MM infarct growth IQR 56-125 mL, eTable 11 gives 56-135 mL.

rows.R: Analysis SAP (supp4 p3, 5.1): 'All analyses will be performed under an as-treated approach.' Report (main p4 Statistical Analysis; Table 1 168/168 vs Table 2 170/166) analyzes treatment comparisons across imaging strata by randomized group (ITT) and within-arm associations as treated. Analysis population for the main treatment-effect comparisons differs from plan; not described as a change. Practical impact limited (2 MM-to-EVT crossovers).
rows.evidence: Supp4 p3-4; main p4, p5 Table 1, p7 Table 2; supp5 p8 flow, p38 eTable 2 (text).
rows.rationale: 168+2 = 170 and 168-2 = 166 reconcile the two analysis sets. The difference is in which set is used for the planned treatment-effect analyses (ITT reported vs as-treated planned). The trial SAP uses ITT, which may explain the choice, but the analysis-specific SAP says as-treated for all analyses.

rows.R: Analysis SAP (supp4 p3, imaging definitions) makes the composite core (larger of CTP/MRI and CT hypodensity) the primary volume and CTP/MRI core a sensitivity analysis; SAP appendix p7 calls composite core 'pre-specified'. Report (main p4, p6; supp5 eFig 10-16) makes CTP/MRI core primary and labels composite-core analyses 'post hoc'; limitations (p10) say the composite concept was preplanned. Primary/sensitivity roles reversed and prespecification mislabeled.
rows.evidence: Supp4 p3, p7; main p1, p4, p6, p8 Fig 3, p10 limitations; supp5 p16 (text).
rows.rationale: Composite (median 101 mL) and CTP/MRI (73 mL) are different measures; the abstract's headline core-volume results use CTP/MRI. The report itself is internally inconsistent about whether composite was prespecified (p4/p6 'post hoc' vs p10 'preplanned'). Retained as a plan-report difference in the primary exposure definition.

rows.R: eFigures 7 and 8 (supp5 p13-14, rendered): ASPECTS 0-2 (n=19) has 0 events in both arms yet prints RR 1.00 (0.37-2.72) for mRS 0-2 and 0-3. With zero events in both arms the modified Poisson RR is not estimable; 0.37-2.72 equals exp(-1) to exp(1), a placeholder. The same figures mark other zero-cell rows '*' (not estimable).
rows.evidence: Supp5 p13, p14 (rendered 170 dpi); main p4 methods; supp4 p4-5.
rows.rationale: exp(-1) = 0.368, exp(1) = 2.718, matching the printed limits exactly. Rows with a single zero arm (e.g., >=150 mL, no mismatch) are shown as '*', so the figure applies two conventions. A printed RR with CI for a stratum without events could be extracted as an informative null and may have entered the ASPECTS interaction tests (P = .9055, .6788); hence substantive.

rows.R: Main p6 (ASPECTS aGenOR 0.91, 0.82-1.00) and p10 (aRR 0.97, 0.93-1.00 per 10 min) call associations significant with upper limits printed as 1.00. Unrounded upper limits in [0.995, 1.0) are compatible with P < .05; log-symmetric reconstruction gives implied upper limits range 0.993-1.027 and 0.996-1.028 within rounding (central 1.010 and 1.012). Not demonstrable beyond rounding.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p4, p6, p7 Table 2, p10 (text).
rows.rationale: R/Python: upper = est^2/lower; 0.905^2/0.825 = 0.993 to 0.915^2/0.815 = 1.027 (central 1.010); 0.965^2/0.935 = 0.996 to 0.975^2/0.925 = 1.028 (central 1.012). Symmetry on the log scale need not hold for PIM or robust Poisson CIs. Because a significant result with an upper limit rounding to 1.00 is possible, there is no demonstrable inconsistency; excluded as a rounding-boundary display. Note outside candidate: Table 2 and p6 expand 'aRR' as 'absolute risk reduction' while the footnote describes a rate ratio.

rows.R: Figure 2B (main p7, rendered): CTP/MRI core >=100 mL, EVT segments 2/6/10/20/10/53% and MM 2/4/16/16/61% show no mRS 4 segment, and mRS 0-2 sums (18%, 6%) contradict eFig 7 (4/51 = 7.8%, 1/49 = 2.0%) and eFig 8 mRS 0-3 (9/51 = 17.6%, 3/49 = 6.1%). Shifting the colors one category reconciles all values and the discussion (~20% ambulation, ~80% mRS >=4). Category labels in panel B are misassigned.
rows.evidence: Main p7 Figure 2 (rendered 220 dpi), p10 discussion; supp5 p13-14 eFig 7-8 (rendered).
rows.rationale: Under the printed colors, EVT mRS 0-2 = 2+6+10 = 18% and 0-3 = 38%. Under a one-category shift (mRS0 2, mRS1 6, mRS2 0, mRS3 10, mRS4 20, mRS5 10, mRS6 53), EVT 0-2 = 8% (4/51 = 7.84%), 0-3 = 18% (9/51 = 17.65%), >=4 = 83%; MM (2, 0, 0, 4, 16, 16, 61): 0-2 = 2% (1/49), 0-3 = 6% (3/49 = 6.12%). Panel A reconciles with eFig 7 (<100 mL: 30/117 = 25.6% vs 2+6+18 = 26%). Figure 2B is the primary-outcome distribution for a key stratum and would be read directly; substantive, direct.

rows.R: Main p8 says that as mismatch volume increased the marginal probability of mRS 0-2 and 0-3 increased with EVT but decreased with MM (eFigure 17). eFigure 17A-B (supp5 p23, rendered): both EVT (cyan) and MM (red) curves decline with increasing mismatch volume; panel C (mRS 5-6) rises in both arms. The narrative contradicts its cited figure.
rows.evidence: Main p8-9 (text); supp5 p23 eFigure 17 (rendered 150 dpi).
rows.rationale: Visual reading: EVT mRS 0-2 falls from about 0.26 at -100 mL to about 0.05 at 380 mL; mRS 0-3 from about 0.63 to 0.07. No alternative axis definition is printed. The statement supports the penumbral interpretation in the discussion, so the contradiction affects interpretation of the mismatch analysis.

rows.R: E changed from statistical_results: this is a conflict over which core-volume variable the age/time prediction surfaces use, not a numerical error. Main p10 and eFigure 18 title (supp5 p24, rendered) say CTP/MRI core set at 70/100/150 mL; eFigure 18 explanation and eFigure 19 (p25) title say composite core. The two measures differ substantially (medians 73 vs 101 mL), so the 150-mL prognostic statement cannot be applied without knowing which.
rows.evidence: Main p3, p10 (text); supp5 p24-25 eFigures 18-19 (rendered 150 dpi).
rows.rationale: The report-internal labels conflict between title, caption and main text. Because the discussion draws a clinical prognostic conclusion ('a patient with a 150-mL core would be unlikely to achieve independent ambulation'), the variable identity matters; rated substantive_inconsistency.

rows.R: Analysis SAP 5.2(3) (supp4 p5) plans predicted probabilities of independent ambulation by age and time from last known well to randomization in EVT patients. Report (main p10; eFig 18-19) uses time from CT perfusion acquisition to reperfusion/end of procedure and LKW to reperfusion/end of procedure. The planned surface is not reported; the time predictor differs.
rows.evidence: Supp4 p5; main p10; supp5 p24-25 (rendered).
rows.rationale: Randomization, imaging and reperfusion are different time anchors; the reported surfaces are not the planned one. Not described as a change.

rows.R: Protocol (supp2, 4 Aug 2021) p8 and p37 call 90-day mRS 0-2 the second primary outcome; p50 calls it the secondary endpoint and lists infarct volume, lesion growth and hospital stay as secondary. Trial SAP (supp3, 20 Nov 2022; OCR p13-14) makes mRS 0-2 secondary and infarct volume, growth and length of stay tertiary. Within-protocol conflict on primary vs secondary status, plus a protocol-SAP change.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p8, p37, p50 (text); supp3 p13-14, p17 (OCR, RapidOCR GPU, confidence >=0.94).
rows.rationale: The within-protocol primary/secondary conflict for mRS 0-2 is a design-element inconsistency affecting multiplicity and hierarchy; the protocol-to-SAP tertiary reassignment may be a later intended revision. This report uses mRS 0-2 as a secondary outcome per the trial SAP and analyzes infarct volume post hoc, so it relies on this hierarchy.

rows.R: Protocol p13 background quotes earlier SELECT cohort results (aOR 2.92, 95% CI 1.00-7.91, P=.041; aOR 2.01, 1.00-4.03, P=.049). These are historical results in the protocol's background, not a design element of this trial or this analysis; lower limits of 1.00 are also compatible with P<.05 after rounding.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p13 (text).
rows.rationale: Plan_material concerns design elements relied on by the reported analysis. Background citations of a prior nonrandomized study do not qualify. Additionally, unrounded lower limits in (1.000, 1.005) would give P<.05, so no inconsistency is demonstrable.

rows.R: Protocol p16 background summarizes earlier SELECT safety results and says sICH (8/173 vs 3/18, P=.072), neurological worsening and mortality 'significantly increased'. Wording imprecision in a background summary of a prior study; not a design element of this trial or analysis.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p16 (text).
rows.rationale: 8/173 = 4.6% and 3/18 = 16.7% reproduce the rounded percentages. Grouping a P=.072 outcome with significant ones is loose wording in background text, outside plan_material scope.

rows.R: Protocol p80-81 and trial SAP p39-40 (OCR) state H_A: P(Y<=X) = 1/2 + theta with Y = MM and X = EVT Rankin score, theta = 0.0791, while lower mRS is better; the orientation appears borrowed from Lai et al. (higher score better). Real notational orientation slip, but it concerns the parent trial's adaptive efficacy test, which this exploratory analysis does not use.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p37, p80-81 (text); supp3 p39-40 (OCR); main p3.
rows.rationale: theta check: (1.95996+1.28155)/sqrt(3*560) = 3.2415/40.988 = 0.0791, reproduces. The direction of claimed efficacy for EVT is unambiguous elsewhere in both plans. No analysis in this report (PIM, modified Poisson within imaging strata) relies on the trial's Wilcoxon interim boundaries or hypothesis orientation; excluded as outside the reported analysis's design elements.

rows.R: Trial SAP (OCR p9, p11-12, p40) schedules efficacy looks at 200 and 380 patients with b = 2.604, but 7.5 reports a DSMB review at 300 patients after which the null was rejected because 'the boundary for efficacy has been crossed', while saying no interim analysis was added. Which boundary/information fraction applied at 300 is not specified. The report (main p4) repeats that the 'prespecified efficacy boundary was crossed'.
rows.evidence: Supp3 p9-12, p39-40 (OCR, confidence >=0.94; p12 checked against rendered PNG); supp2 p45-48; main p4.
rows.rationale: 300 is not a rounded version of 200 or 380. The plan materials do not define a rule for an unscheduled look, so whether stopping was consistent with the prespecified design cannot be determined from the supplied documents. This bears on the analysis population (352 enrolled at stopping) described in the report, so retained; K indeterminate.

rows.R: Analysis SAP (supp4 p5) defines sICH as PH2/remote PH with >=4-point NIHSS increase at a 4-hour window; trial SAP (OCR p13, p18, p31) defines SITS-MOST sICH as >=4-point NIHSS increase or death within 24 hours. Window and death component differ; the report (main p3) cites SITS-MOST and eTable 2 gives 0/168 vs 2/168 without stating which definition applied.
rows.evidence: Supp4 p5 (text); supp3 p13, p18, p31 (OCR); main p3; supp5 p38 eTable 2 (text).
rows.rationale: 4 h vs 24 h and inclusion of death are material definitional differences for a safety outcome. '4-hour' may be a typographic slip for 24 hours, but the documents do not show this. Counts are small, so numerical impact is likely small, but the definition is not determinable.

rows.R: Analysis SAP 5.3.3 (supp4 p6) plans stratification by mismatch volume thresholds of 50 and 100 mL with the 5.2 outcome analyses. Searched main and supp5 (eFig 7-13, 20; eTables 7-10): only the 1.2/10 and 1.8/15 ratio-volume profiles and continuous mismatch volume (eFig 17) are reported. The planned 50/100-mL strata are not reported.
rows.evidence: Supp4 p4, p6; main p1, p6-8; supp5 contents and eFigure 20 subpanel list, p23, p43 (text search).
rows.rationale: Text search of supp5 for mismatch-volume strata found none at 50 or 100 mL; eFigure 20 subpanels list only ratio-volume profiles. Planned analysis absent from the report package.

rows.R: eFigure 13 (supp5 p19, rendered): outcome is mRS 5-6 (adverse), RR = EVT vs MM, all 16 RRs < 1 (0.55-0.87), yet the axis labels the side below 1 'Favours Medical Management'. For an adverse outcome RR < 1 favors thrombectomy. Labels reversed; counts and RRs are clear.
rows.evidence: Supp5 p19 eFigure 13 (rendered 150 dpi); p15 eFigure 9 convention; main p3.
rows.rationale: Counts confirm lower adverse rates with EVT (e.g., 27/68 39.7% vs 39/64 60.9%). The direction label is wrong but the numeric results and caption allow correct reading; minor presentation.

rows.R: Discordant profile 2 (ASPECTS 6-10, core >=70 mL): eTable 9 (supp5 p47-48) gives MM mRS 0-3 3/11 and mRS 5-6 10/11 (sum 13 > 11) with MM median 6 (6-6); eTable 10 gives MM 4/12 and 11/12 (15 > 12), and 2/12 + 11/12 = 13 > 12. eTable 8 instead gives EVT 1/12 and 3/12 favorable and MM 0/11, i.e., favorable counts sit in the opposite arm in eTable 9.
rows.evidence: Supp5 p45-50 eTables 8-10 (text, layout checked).
rows.rationale: mRS 0-3 and 5-6 are disjoint, so counts summing above the denominator are impossible. Cross-table: eTable 8 EVT 1/12 (mRS 0-2), 3/12 (0-3); eTable 9 MM 1/11, 3/11 and EVT 0/12, 0/12 - arm columns appear swapped for favorable outcomes. Extracted subgroup counts would be wrong in at least one table; substantive, direct.

rows.R: Protocol (Aug 2021) p48 permits subgroup selection and testing after failure of the final overall efficacy test; trial SAP v1.0.0 (Nov 2022; OCR p10) declares no superiority on final failure without that branch. A real version difference, but it concerns a final-analysis branch of the parent trial that was never executed (trial stopped at 300) and on which this exploratory analysis does not rely.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p45-48 (text); supp3 p9-10, p12, p40 (OCR).
rows.rationale: Plan_material requires a design element the reported analysis relies on. The final-stage adaptive rescue branch has no bearing on any analysis in this report. Excluded as outside scope rather than as non-existent.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p5, Primary Analysis): 'All estimates will be adjusted for baseline confounders.' Report (main p4) uses ordinary logistic regression with no covariates named; printed primary RR 1.35 and OR 1.57 equal the crude values (287/759)/(208/744) = 1.353 and (287*536)/(472*208) = 1.567. The primary estimate is unadjusted; not described as a change (amendment list p15 is silent).
rows.evidence: Supp1 p5-6, p15 (text); main p1, p4-5; supp2 p14 eTable 5 (text).
rows.rationale: R: RR = 1.3525, OR = 1.5669, both matching the printed values exactly, which supports an unadjusted model. In a randomized trial both are valid, but the plan specified covariate adjustment, which changes the OR estimand (conditional vs marginal). Retained as a plan-report difference in the primary model.

rows.R: Main p2 says the waitlist group was not included in tests of statistical significance, but the retention P values on p4 (P=.02 at 1 month, P=.11 at 7 months) reproduce only as 3-group tests including waitlist (chi-square P = .017 and .115). Two-group tests (intervention vs assessment-only) give P = .007 and .064. Conclusions about retention are unchanged.

rows.R: Original protocol V2.0 (supp2 p11, p41): 686 patients and 91 events. 91 equals the Schoenfeld event count for 90% power (90.3), whereas 686 with 12.2%/6.25% one-year risks yields about 63 events, consistent with the 80% power stated on p41 (67 events required). The original design is internally loose (90% vs 80%), but it was superseded by the final V2.3 design of 512 patients with new assumptions, which the reported analysis uses.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p11-12, p18, p40-41; final protocol and SAP v2.0 sample-size text (lines 4149-4152, 6056, 9102-9104) (text).
rows.rationale: R: 4*(qnorm(.975)+qnorm(.9))^2/log(6.45/12.76)^2 = 90.3; with 80% power 67.5; expected one-year events 343*0.122 + 343*0.0625 = 63.3. The 91 is a required-event target, not a forecast, and longer follow-up (up to 3 years) could supply it. The original sample-size section is not a design element of the reported analysis, which follows the amended 512-patient design (change disclosed in the version log). Excluded.

rows.R: Table 3 (main p9) ED visits: absolute difference 3.38 per 100 patient-weeks (95% CrI -0.57 to 7.94) and RR 1.72 (95% CI 1.03-2.87), P=.04. Different models and inferential frameworks; no contradiction.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p4, p6, p9 Table 3 and footnote b (text); supp2 p17 eTable 12, p22 eMethods.
rows.rationale: The P value belongs to the RR model and agrees with its CI (both exclude the null). The CrI is from a differently specified model and is explicitly labeled. An inference that differs across models is a substantive point for interpretation (the ED finding is fragile), but it is not a reporting inconsistency. Excluded.

rows.R: eTable 10 (supp2 p13-14), severe mouth sores (SSPedi>=3): intervention 0/0 vs control 2/8 and 1/8, with ORs 2.6 (0.04-170.4) and 5.00 (0.07-366.4), P>.99. An OR cannot be estimated with an empty arm. Values reproduce exactly with a 0.5 continuity correction (Haldane-Woolf), which is not described; footnote b names logistic regression.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p13-15 eTable 10 and footnotes, p22 eMethods (text).
rows.rationale: R: (0.5*6.5)/(0.5*2.5) = 2.6, CI 0.04-170.39; (0.5*7.5)/(0.5*1.5) = 5.0, CI 0.07-366.35. Other all-zero rows (e.g., 0/26 vs 0/56, OR 2.13) follow the same correction. The printed estimates are artifacts of an unstated correction, but the counts and the extreme CIs make clear that there is no information; minor.

rows.R: Sadness any-intervention, all participants (supp2 p13; main p5): OR 0.51 (0.26-0.99), P=.05, called significant under the P<.05 rule. An unrounded P in [.045, .05) is compatible with an upper limit of 0.99; the displayed P is a rounding boundary, not a demonstrable inconsistency.
rows.evidence: Main p4-5; supp2 p13, p15 footnote b (text).
rows.rationale: The CI excluding 1 indicates P<.05 under the same model; P printed to 2 decimals as .05 is consistent with e.g. .048. Displaying '.05' while calling it significant is imprecise but not an error that changes a value or conclusion. Excluded as rounding.

rows.R: eTable 10 (supp2 p14), symptom-specific intervention among those with SSPedi>=1: neuropathy 6/57 vs 0/70, OR 17.8 (0.98-323.1), P=.007; hunger 6/111 vs 0/130, OR 16.08 (0.9-288.74), P=.009. CIs include 1 while P<.05; main p6 calls both significant. The ORs/CIs reproduce exactly with a 0.5-corrected Woolf interval and the P values exactly with Fisher's exact test (.00702, .00886), not with the logistic regression named in footnote b.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p14-15 eTable 10 and footnote b, p22 eMethods; main p5-6 (text).
rows.rationale: R: Haldane-Woolf 17.8 (0.98, 323.06) and 16.08 (0.90, 288.74); Fisher P 0.00702 and 0.00886. Ordinary logistic regression cannot give a finite MLE with a zero cell (Wald P about 1; LRT P = .0016 for neuropathy). The row pairs an interval and a test from different methods without saying so. The significance claim is supported by Fisher's test, which is a valid choice for sparse data and matches the plan's stated test, so interpretation is largely preserved; minor.

rows.R: Abstract (main p1): 'Among the 338 randomized infants ..., 320 underwent operative repair'. 320 = 163 + 157 infants remaining after 9 withdrawals per group (Table 1, p4). Surgery characteristics (p4-5) give 152 early + 129 late = 281 who underwent repair; 11 early and 28 late infants did not. The abstract mislabels the post-withdrawal cohort as the operated population.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p3 Figure 1, p4-5 Table 1 and Surgery Characteristics (text).

That 18% of the late group never needed repair (17 resolved) is part of the clinical case for late repair, and the abstract statement obscures it; the demographics that follow describe the 320, not an operated cohort. Rated substantive for interpretation; the count is unlikely to be an extraction input.

rows.R: SAP (supp2 p8-9): intervention prior for categorical outcomes OR 1.0 with 95% CrI 0.2-4 (Normal(0, SD 0.7) on log OR; exp(+/-1.96*0.7) = 0.25-3.94); count outcomes RR 0.33-3.3; interaction terms Normal(0, SD 0.6) (0.31-3.24). The primary posterior probability (97%) was close to the 95% stopping/benefit threshold, so prior width is not immaterial. Which prior was actually used cannot be determined from the documents; recorded as a plan-report difference.

rows.R: Subgroup eFigure (supp3 p2, rendered): legend labels the plotted intervals '99% CI', the caption says the numbers on the right are relative risks with 95% CIs, and the plotted lines coincide with the printed numeric intervals (e.g., low ERAS 0.49-2.08). rows.R: Abstract (p1) says patients were 'randomly assigned 1:1 to restrictive (n = 733) or liberal (n = 724)'; Key Points (p2) say 'Among 1508 randomized adult trauma patients'. Figure 1 (p3) and Results (p5): 1979 randomized (983 restrictive, 994 liberal after 2 lost envelopes), 1508 completed (750/758), 733/724 in the primary analysis. 733/724 are analyzed and 1508 completed patients, not randomized counts.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p2 Key Points, p3 Figure 1, p5 Trial Population, p8 limitations (text).

Randomized arm sizes are standard extraction inputs for attrition/risk-of-bias assessment; substantive, direct.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p13, p26; final p49, p62): include up to 1600 participants and stop when 1420 evaluable participants with 30-day follow-up are reached. SAP (p85) and main p5: 1420 including a 3.5% dropout; main p5 also says the trial ends after 1420 evaluable patients. Realized: 1979 randomized, 1508 completed, 1457 with primary outcome. Whether 1600 referred to randomized or retained participants, and whether 1420 is evaluable or includes dropouts, is not defined consistently.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p13, p26, p49, p62, p85; main p3 Figure 1, p5 (text).
rows.rationale: If 1600 meant randomized participants, 1979 exceeds it by 379; if it meant retained participants, 1508 is within it. 1457 primary-available exceeds 1420 under either target definition. The documents describe the populations inconsistently and the conduct cannot be judged against the accrual cap; L indeterminate.

rows.R: Protocols (supp1 p13, p23-24; final p49, p59-60) list secondary outcomes without hierarchy. SAP (p85-89; approved 11 Jan 2023 while still recruiting, before export) designates 30-day mortality and major respiratory complications as key secondary outcomes and the rest as exploratory with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control; the report follows the SAP (main p5-6; supp2 eTables 4-6). Outcome-status change relative to the protocol, documented prospectively in the SAP.
rows.rationale: Difference between protocol and report in outcome hierarchy and multiplicity handling; the SAP documents the change before analysis (per fixed review decision, a documented change is still retained as a difference). Long-term outcomes are explicitly deferred and not counted.

rows.R: Protocols (supp1 p26, p62): primary analysis adjusted for age, sex, centre, intubation at randomization and known pneumonia on admission. SAP (p88) and report (main p5; supp2 eTables 4, 8): adjusted for stratification variables (site, intubation), with an additional model adding age, sex, ISS and first GCS; no model includes pneumonia on admission. Covariate set changed; documented in the SAP.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p26, p62, p84, p88-89; main p5; supp2 p17, p22 (text).
rows.rationale: Primary OR 1.01 (0.75-1.37) and additional OR 0.98 (0.68-1.41) come from models other than the protocol's. Retained as a primary-model covariate difference, documented prospectively in the SAP.

rows.R: SAP subgroup list (supp1 p89) includes 'Episode(s) of hypoxaemia during the intervention (SpO2 <90%)' for the primary outcome; main methods (p5), Figure 4 (p8) and eTable 7 (supp2 p20-21) report six subgroups (intubation, ICU, TBI, lung disease, inclusion site, ISS) and no hypoxemia subgroup.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p26, p62, p89; main p5, p8; supp2 p17-25 (text).
rows.rationale: Planned subgroup analysis absent without explanation. Note that hypoxemia during the intervention is a postrandomization variable, which may explain omission, but this is not stated.

rows.R: Protocols (supp1 p26, p62) and SAP (p89) define the intubation subgroup as 'initially intubated within one hour after trauma'; Figure 4 (p8) and eTable 7 (supp2 p20) use 'intubated at randomization' (the stratification variable). Median trauma-to-randomization time was 54 vs 52 min (IQR to 79 min), so membership could differ for some patients; extent unknown.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p26, p62, p89; main p5, p8; supp2 p16, p20-21 (text).
rows.rationale: The subgroup definition differs in its time anchor. Because about a quarter of patients were randomized more than an hour after trauma, some reclassification is possible, but the documents give no cross-tabulation; L indeterminate.

rows.R: Protocols (supp1 p26, p62): categorical secondary outcomes (including 30-day mortality and major respiratory complications) compared with Fisher's exact/chi-square tests. SAP (p88-89) and report (main p5; supp2 eTable 4): logistic regression with GEE and inverse probability weighting, ORs adjusted for stratification variables. Method changed; documented in the SAP.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p23, p26, p59, p62, p88-89; main p5-6; supp2 p17 (text).
rows.rationale: Unadjusted categorical tests vs adjusted weighted ORs are different analyses. Death OR 1.28 (0.85-1.92), P=.23; respiratory OR 0.84 (0.59-1.19), P=.33; conclusions unlikely to change, but the analysis differs from the protocol.

rows.R: SSI (main Figure 2 p6; supp2 eTable 5 p18): OR 0.50 (0.25-0.99), P=.05 (additional models P=.03, .04) while the risk difference -3.04 (-6.87 to 0.79) includes 0. The OR is from the stratification-adjusted GEE logistic model; the RD comes from a separate, unspecified model. Different estimands and models can give different null readings near the boundary; the report correctly states that no exploratory outcome was significant after FDR control.
rows.evidence: Main p5-6 Figure 2; supp2 p18 eTable 5; supp1 p86 (text).
rows.rationale: Not a demonstrable contradiction. Outside this candidate: the crude SSI risk difference is 23/736 - 32/724 = 3.13% - 4.42% = -1.29 points, and RDs in Figure 2 depart from crude differences in both directions (primary +0.56 vs crude -0.61; MRC -0.61 vs crude -1.92); the RD method is not described, which limits interpretation of the RD column.

rows.R: SAP Table 4 (supp1 p101): SSI = purulent drainage, OR positive microbiologic testing AND signs of infection, OR surgeon diagnosis. Results supplement 3.3.2 (supp2 p9): drainage, OR positive microbiology (alone), OR deliberate opening by a surgeon AND signs, OR surgeon diagnosis ('further elaborations'). The reported definition is broader.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p84, p100-101; supp2 p9, p18; main p6 Figure 2 (text).
rows.rationale: Microbiology without signs, and opening plus signs, qualify only under the reported definition. SSI is the exploratory outcome with the smallest P value (OR 0.50, P=.05), so the definition matters for interpretation.

rows.R: ICU subgroup in Figure 4/eTable 7 (Yes 271 and 238; No 458 and 481) does not match the exploratory 'ICU admission' outcome (374/738, 359/736), but it matches the Table's 'destination after trauma resuscitation: ICU' (276/741, 242/739) restricted to the primary-analysis set (733/724). The subgroup is the immediate ICU destination; the outcome counts any ICU admission. Label is imprecise but the numbers reconcile.
rows.evidence: Main p4 Table (destination rows), p5, p8 Figure 4; supp2 p18, p20 (text).
rows.rationale: 271 + 458 = 729 of 733 and 238 + 481 = 719 of 724 (a few unclassified), and 271 <= 276, 238 <= 242. The apparent mismatch arises from comparing two different ICU variables. Excluded; the subgroup label could state 'immediate ICU destination'.

rows.R: Liberal AIS <3 primary-outcome cell: eTable 7 (supp2 p20) 48/473 (9.2%) vs main Figure 4 (p8) 48/473 (10.1%). 48/473 = 10.15%; the supplement percentage is wrong.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p20-21 (text); main p8 Figure 4 (text).
rows.rationale: 100*48/473 = 10.148. Count and the main-text percentage agree; typographic error in the supplement. Note: AIS <3 restrictive 45/500 (9.0%) reproduces.

rows.R: eTable 1 (supp2 p14) receiving center Bern: 50/750 (7.2%) and 47/758 (6.7%); 50/750 = 6.7% and 47/758 = 6.2%. Other receiving-center percentages are also slightly off (Rigshospitalet 335/750 = 44.7% printed 44.4; 348/758 = 45.9% printed 45.7; Odense 173/750 = 23.1% printed 22.9), while counts sum to 750 and 758, suggesting percentages were computed from a different data version.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p14 eTable 1 (text).
rows.rationale: Computed: 6.67, 6.20, 44.67, 45.91, 23.07, 23.35 (%). Percentages in the column sum to 100.0 but do not match the counts; counts are internally consistent. Descriptive baseline display; minor.

rows.R: eTable 2 (supp2 p15) liberal walk-in transport: 4/743 (5.3%); 4/743 = 0.54%. The liberal transport percentages sum to 104.7% with 5.3 and to 99.9% with 0.5, so 5.3 is a misprint for 0.5.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p15 eTable 2 (text).
rows.rationale: Liberal counts 585+141+9+3+4+1 = 743 (counts reconcile). 78.7+19.0+1.2+0.4+0.1 = 99.4, + 0.5 = 99.9. Typographic error in a baseline descriptive cell.

rows.R: eTable 2 (supp2 p15) liberal vascular surgery in the trauma room: 0/747 (1.1%). A zero numerator cannot give 1.1%; one of the two values is wrong. Outside this candidate, the firearm injury row uses denominator 724 (8/724) where all other restrictive mechanism rows use 742.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p15 eTable 2 (text).
rows.rationale: 0/747 = 0.0%. Possibly a value shifted from the cardiothoracic row (9/747 = 1.2%) or similar; cannot be resolved. Descriptive baseline display; minor.

rows.R: eTable 10 (supp2 p24): exclusion after randomization 55/750 (45%) and 67/758 (55%); secondary exclusion 174/750 (51%) and 165/758 (49%). The percentages are shares of the excluded patients (55/122 = 45%, 174/339 = 51%), not of the printed denominators (55/750 = 7.3%, 174/750 = 23.2%). Also row N=130 vs 55+67 = 122 is unexplained (the footnote explains only the secondary-exclusion row).
rows.evidence: Supp2 p24 eTable 10 (text); main p3 Figure 1.
rows.rationale: Computed: 55/122 = 45.1, 67/122 = 54.9, 174/339 = 51.3, 165/339 = 48.7; 55/750 = 7.3, 67/758 = 8.8, 174/750 = 23.2, 165/758 = 21.8. The title signals a distribution among excluded patients, so the intended meaning is recoverable; the n/N (%) format is misleading. Also, the 750/758 denominators are the completed cohort, from which these patients were by definition excluded. Minor.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p7, p24-25, p28-30) rerandomizes week-6 nonabstainers to continue, switch or increase, with continuation as the reference. Report (main p1, p4, p6 Figure 2 footnote c, p8 limitation) adds 40 CNRT and 35 varenicline nonabstainers who did not attend rerandomization to the continuation arms (90 = 50 + 40; 77 = 42 + 35). Nonrandomized participants enter only the reference arms. Disclosed in the report as an intention-to-treat choice.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p7, p24-25, p28-30; main p1, p4, p6, p8; supp2 p6, p19 (text).
rows.rationale: The phase-2 comparisons are no longer purely randomized: 40/90 and 35/77 continuation participants were not randomized and were nonreturners (likely to be counted as smoking), which can bias the continuation reference downward and inflate rescue-strategy benefits. Disclosed (main p4, p8), retained as a difference per the fixed review decision. Note: main p4 says these participants 'did attend rerandomization', contradicting the abstract and Figure 2 ('did not').

rows.R: Supplement eAppendix 3 (supp2 p5-6) gives inverse probability weights 2 for phase-1 abstainers and 1/(0.5*0.33) = 6.06 for rerandomized nonabstainers, but does not say how the 75 nonrandomized nonreturners assigned to continuation (40 CNRT, 35 varenicline) were weighted. They make up 40/90 and 35/77 of the reference arms of the primary contrasts, so the primary estimates depend on an unstated weighting rule.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p5-6, p19; main p1, p4, p6 Figure 2 (text).
rows.rationale: 1/0.5 = 2; 1/(0.5*0.33) = 6.06 reproduce. No probability exists for a deterministic, nonrandomized assignment, so the weight used is undefined in the report. Because these participants dominate the continuation arms, the weighting choice affects the primary risk differences; substantive. Cannot recompute without the rule.

rows.R: Abstract (p1) phase-2 allocation percentages mix denominators: CNRT continue 90 (47%) = 90/191, increase 50 (33%) = 50/151, switch 51 (34%) = 51/151; varenicline increase 39 (32%) = 39/122, switch 41 (34%) = 41/122, continue 77 (49%) = 77/157. Each arm's percentages sum to 114-115%.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p6 Figure 2 (text).
rows.rationale: Computed: 90/191 = 47.1, 50/151 = 33.1, 51/151 = 33.8, 51/191 = 26.7; 39/122 = 32.0, 41/122 = 33.6, 77/157 = 49.0, 41/157 = 26.1. Counts are correct; percentages use different denominators within the same sentence. Presentation only.

rows.R: Abstract (p1): CNRT rescue strategies vs continuation, absolute RD 6% (95% CrI 6% to 11%); main p5 gives 6% (2%-11%) for both switching and dose increase, and eTable 4 (supp2 p21) gives 6% (2%-11%) and 6% (2%-10%). The abstract's lower limit equals the point estimate and is wrong.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p5 (text); supp2 p21 eTable 4 (text).
rows.rationale: Lower limit 6 vs 2 percentage points for the primary contrast. A CrI whose lower bound equals the median is implausible for these counts (7/51, 7/50 vs 7/90). The abstract interval for a primary result would be extracted directly; substantive.

rows.R: Varenicline nonabstainers: switch to CNRT 0% (0/41) vs continue 3% (2/77). Main p5: switching to CNRT 'resulted in an absolute RD of -3% ... posterior probability >99% that continuing was worse than switching'; the abstract attaches -3% to 'continuing ... was worse than switching to a higher dosage'. eTable 4 (supp2 p21) prints switch-vs-stay +3% (+1% to +4%). The sign and the stated direction conflict; per the arm probabilities, switching was worse than continuing.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p5, p7 Figure 3, p8 discussion (text); supp2 p21 eTable 4 (text).
rows.rationale: Switch 0% minus continue 3% = -3 points, so switching is worse; 'continuing was worse than switching' reverses the direction, and the abstract wording conflates the switch contrast with the dose-increase contrast (RD 18%). The eTable sign convention (+3) is opposite to the text (-3). A reader of the abstract would misread which strategy is inferior; substantive.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p31): a posterior probability > 0.90 that the effect exists 'constitutes sufficient evidence'; power prose p33 refers to detecting 0.90. Report (main p4; supp2 p9) describes > 0.80 as the prespecified posterior probability sufficient to confirm the hypotheses. The decision threshold called prespecified differs from the plan.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p31, p33-34; main p4; supp2 p8-9, p18 (text).
rows.rationale: Plan Table 3 tabulates 0.80-0.95 as scenarios but selects 0.90. The primary results exceed 0.99, so conclusions are unaffected, but the 'prespecified' label is not supported by the supplied plan. Note the protocol supplied is dated 23 Aug 2023, after trial completion.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p28): secondary joint modeling of outcomes and missingness, missing-data sensitivity analyses with pattern-mixture models, and sensitivity analyses with optimistic, pessimistic and skeptical priors. None is reported in the main article or supplement (only missing = smoking, a convergence-driven intercept prior change, and post hoc GEE dynamic-treatment estimates).
rows.evidence: Supp1 p28; main p4, p7-8; supp2 contents and pp5-13 (text).
rows.rationale: Planned robustness analyses of the primary model are absent. The intercept prior change (supp2 p8) was for convergence, not a planned prior sensitivity analysis.

rows.R: EOT+30 continuous abstinence, varenicline continuation: main p7 and supp2 p10 give '0%; n = 42', but the continuation arm in the primary-analysis framework is 77 (42 rerandomized + 35 assigned), and eFigure 2 (supp2 p15) prints 0/77. The n label is inconsistent with the analyzed population.
rows.evidence: Main p6-7; supp2 p10, p15 (text).
rows.rationale: 42 + 35 = 77. The 0% estimate is the same either way; only the sample size label is wrong. The CNRT continuation counterpart is correctly n = 90 in the same sentence. Minor.

rows.R: Six-month continuous abstinence: main p7 and supp2 p10 say only CNRT dose increase (3%) and varenicline dose increase (2%) provided benefit over continuation (0%). Detailed results (supp2 p11) and eFigure 3 (p16) give CNRT increase 6% (3/50) and continuation 3% (3/90), ARD 3% (eTable 9). The CNRT figures in the summary are risk differences presented as arm probabilities.
rows.evidence: Main p7; supp2 p10-11, p16 eFigure 3, p33 eTable 9 (text).
rows.rationale: 6% - 3% = 3% (the ARD), mislabeled as the increase arm with continuation at 0%. For varenicline, increase 2% vs continuation 0% are arm values (ARD also 2%), so the summary mixes quantities. Arm-level secondary outcome rates in the main text are wrong for CNRT; substantive for extraction.

rows.R: Protocol Figure 2 (supp1 p31-32), repeated in supplement eFigure 1 (supp2 p14): week-6 design inputs CNRT 0.48 (0.38-0.58) Beta(193, 210) and varenicline 0.50 (0.40-0.60) Beta(785, 869). Quantiles of these betas are 0.430-0.528 and 0.451-0.499 (medians 0.479, 0.475). The eight week-12 boxes reproduce from their betas. The week-6 intervals and beta parameters are inconsistent.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p31-34; supp2 p5, p14 (text).
rows.rationale: R qbeta(c(.025,.5,.975), 193, 210) = 0.430, 0.479, 0.528; qbeta(..., 785, 869) = 0.451, 0.475, 0.499. Which inputs drove the simulations is unknown, but these are planning inputs for power simulation, not for the reported analysis; minor.

rows.R: Supp2 p8: revised intercept prior 'Normal(mean = 0, variance = 10)' on the log-odds scale, with stated 95% prior interval for the odds 3.07 x 10^-9 to 325,215,956. exp(+/-1.96*sqrt(10)) = 0.0020 to 492; the printed interval equals exp(+/-1.96*10), i.e., SD = 10 (variance 100). The prior is misstated.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p7-8 (text).
rows.rationale: R: exp(c(-1,1)*1.959964*sqrt(10)) = 0.00203, 491.74; exp(c(-1,1)*1.96*10) = 3.07e-09, 3.25e+08. Either variance or interval is wrong. Both priors are diffuse relative to plausible intercepts, so posterior estimates are unlikely to be sensitive, but the prior must be stated correctly; minor.

rows.R: Supplement eAppendix 4 narrative (supp2 p10-11) prints EOT+30 estimates with shifted decimals: '1.0% (7.0%-1.3%)' for 10% (7%-13%) in eFigure 2; '8.0% (5.0%-1.1%)' (four times) for 8% (5%-11%); '6.0% (3.0%-1.0%)' for 6% (3%-10%); '1.1% (-1.0%-22%)' for 11% (-1%-22%) in eTable 11. Figures and tables are correct.
rows.rationale: Point estimates lie outside or at the edge of reversed intervals, a decimal-scale formatting error repeated across seven occurrences; matched figure/table values are consistent with counts. Supplementary narrative only; minor.

rows.R: Six-month continuous abstinence among phase-1 abstainers, CNRT vs varenicline: supp2 p12 narrative ARD 1.0% (-1.3% to 1.1%), probability 55%; eTable 11 (p35) ARD 1% (-11% to 12%), probability 56%. Arm probabilities 39% (30-48) and 40% (33-47) make the eTable interval plausible; the narrative limits are wrong (decimal slip, cf. C012).
rows.evidence: Supp2 p12, p16, p35 (text).
rows.rationale: With arm CrIs spanning about 18 and 14 points, an ARD CrI of width about 23 points (eTable) is coherent and one of width 2.4 points is not. Secondary, supplementary; minor.

rows.R: Supplement eFigure 1 (supp2 p14) defines the CNRT dose-increase design cell as two 21-mg patches plus 4-mg lozenges; eTables 1-2 (p17-18), main p4, Figure 3 caption and the protocol (supp1 p25) specify 2-mg lozenges. Main p8 notes 2-mg rather than 4-mg lozenges were used as a practical choice, so eFigure 1 may reflect an earlier assumption.
rows.evidence: Supp2 p14-18; main p4, p7-8; supp1 p25 (text).
rows.rationale: The conflict concerns the label of a design-simulation input, not the delivered intervention, which is consistently 2 mg elsewhere. Meaning recoverable; minor.

rows.R: Key Points (main p2) give the primary between-group difference as 0.30 (95% CI -6.9 to 6.4); abstract (p1), Table 2 (p6), Results (p7) and eTable 4 (supp3 p5) give -0.3 with the same CI (eTable 1: -0.27). The table convention is placebo change minus krill change: -20.2 - (-19.9) = -0.3.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p2, p6-7; supp3 p2, p5 (text).
rows.rationale: Sign error in Key Points only; the CI is symmetric around about -0.25, so +0.30 is inconsistent with its own interval center. Null result unaffected; minor.

rows.R: Placebo omega-3 content: Methods (main p2-3) 'less than 5 mg/g (0.5%)'; Discussion (p9) 'less than 5 mg/g (0.05%)'. 5 mg/g = 0.5%; the Discussion percentage is off by a factor of 10.
rows.evidence: Main p2-3, p9 (text).
rows.rationale: 5 mg / 1000 mg = 0.005 = 0.5%. Typographic decimal error in describing the placebo; no outcome is affected.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p8): primary VAS pain asked as 'how would you rate your pain today'. Report (main p3, Table 1 footnote b): knee pain VAS 'over the past 7 days'. The recall period of the primary outcome differs; not described as a change.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p2, p6, p8; main p3, p5 (text).
rows.rationale: Current pain vs past-week pain are different constructs with different variability; the primary outcome definition changed (or one document is wrong). Retained.

rows.R: Table 1 footnote g (main p5): ICOAP has 5 constant-pain questions and 8 intermittent-pain questions; Methods (p4): items scored 0-4, constant 0-20, intermittent 0-24, total 0-44. 5 x 4 = 20, but 8 x 4 = 32 and 13 x 4 = 52; the ranges imply 6 intermittent items (11 total). The item count in the footnote is wrong.
rows.evidence: Main p4, p5 Table 1 footnote g, p6 (text).
rows.rationale: Ranges 0-24 and 0-44 are consistent with 6 intermittent items; the footnote's '8' conflicts. Also the response labels differ between p4 ('never'...'very often') and the footnote ('not at all'...'extremely'). Post hoc outcome, rescaled to 0-100; minor.

rows.R: Protocol power (supp1 p2, p12): 10-mm VAS difference, SD of change 25.5 (4Jointz data), 90% power, 234 + 10% = 260; effusion: 96% power for a 20% difference in effusion area (mean 2.24 cm2, SD 1.35). Report (main p4): 130/group for 90% power to detect 10 points with SD 23.8 and a 4.5-mL effusion-volume change. Inputs and the effusion metric (area vs volume) differ.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p2, p12; main p4 (text).
rows.rationale: R power.t.test: SD 25.5, 117/group, delta 10 -> power 0.848 (90% needs 138/group); SD 23.8, 130/group -> 0.921. The reported power statement does not match the protocol's inputs; the report's SD gives the stated power with 130/group. Difference in design specification, not disclosed.

rows.R: Protocol/SAP excerpt (supp1 p12; supp2 p1): linear regression comparing changes between groups (multivariable if baseline imbalance), missing data handled by propensity weighting. Report (main p4, p7): linear mixed model with treatment, month and treatment x month, random intercepts for participant and centre and random slope for month, all available data; age-missingness sensitivity analysis. Primary model and missing-data approach differ.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p12; supp2 p1; main p4, p7; supp3 p2 eTable 1 (text).
rows.rationale: Repeated-measures mixed model using all time points vs single change-score regression with propensity weighting are different analyses (and handle missing data under different assumptions). Not described as a change.

rows.R: Protocol/SAP (supp1 p12; supp2 p1 lines 8-9): per-protocol analyses for participants consuming >=80% of capsules. Report reports adherence (95% took >=80%, main p7; eTable 2) but no per-protocol efficacy estimate for the primary outcome in the main text or supplement.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p12; supp2 p1; main p4, p6-7; supp3 pp1-15 (text).
rows.rationale: Unconditionally planned per-protocol analysis absent. With 95% adherent, results would likely be similar, but the analysis is not reported.

rows.R: Point contrasts that do not match their arm changes under the table's placebo-minus-krill convention: ICOAP total 24 wk, -8.2 - (-9.9) = 1.7 vs printed 2.05 (main p6); WOMAC weight-bearing pain week 4 arm changes -84 and -103 (supp3 p5) are inconsistent with their own final/baseline means (100 - 127 = -27; 108 - 141 = -33) and with the contrast 3; hsCRP 12 wk, 0.24 - (-0.53) = 0.77 vs printed 0.07 (-1.19 to 1.33), P=.92, the same tuple printed for glucose 12 wk (supp3 p6).
rows.evidence: Main p6 Table 2; supp3 p5-6 eTable 4 (text).
rows.rationale: Convention verified on other rows: primary -20.2 - (-19.9) = -0.3; ICOAP intermittent -8.2 - (-9.7) = 1.5; hsCRP 24 wk -0.12 - (-0.76) = 0.64. The WOMAC week-4 arm changes are implausible against adjacent weeks (week 8: -37/-36). The hsCRP 12-week contrast appears copied from the glucose row. Several secondary-outcome values in the tables are wrong and would be extracted as printed; substantive for data use, though conclusions (no effect) are unchanged.

rows.R: Main Table 3 (p8) vs eTable 7 (supp3 p10-11, rendered): cough krill 2/placebo 0 vs eTable blank/2; gastroesophageal reflux 1/3 vs 3/1; abdominal discomfort 0/3 vs 3/blank. eTable 7 subrows sum to the GI totals (krill 13, placebo 6); the main-table subrows attribute these events to the wrong arm. Also outside this candidate: Table 3 'pain in extremity' placebo 6 vs 5 in abstract, text and eTable 7; 'participants with an adverse event' 67 (50.7%) should be 67/130 = 51.5%.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p8 Table 3; supp3 p10-11 eTable 7 (text and rendered 110 dpi).
rows.rationale: eTable 7 GI krill: 3+1+1+1+1+3+1+1+1 = 13; placebo: 2+1+1+1+1 = 6, matching main totals; the main-table subrow attributions are reversed for 3 events types. Since the paper highlights more GI events with krill oil, misattributing specific GI events matters for safety interpretation; substantive.

rows.R: Main text (p8) and Table 3 footnote: all serious adverse events were considered unrelated to treatment. eTable 8 (supp3 p14, rendered) classifies relationship with treatment: krill oil transfusion-dependent anaemia 'Probable', six other krill SAEs and three placebo SAEs 'Possible'; only 2 'Unlikely' and 2 'NA'. The main safety statement contradicts the supplementary classification.
rows.evidence: Main p1, p8 Table 3 and footnote; supp3 p14 eTable 8 (rendered 150 dpi).
rows.rationale: A 'Probable' treatment relationship for a severe SAE in the active arm is not compatible with 'all events were considered unrelated'. Omega-3 supplementation has plausible bleeding-related effects, so this is safety-relevant; substantive.

rows.R: Protocol (supp1 p12): 96% power to detect a 20% difference in effusion size (mean 2.24 cm2, SD of change 1.35) with 130/group (or 117 evaluable). A two-sample calculation with delta = 0.448 cm2 and SD 1.35 gives about 72% (117/group) to 76% (130/group). The stated power cannot be reproduced from the stated inputs; an unstated assumption (e.g., a different SD scale) may explain it.
rows.evidence: Supp1 p2, p12; supp2 p1 (text).
rows.rationale: R: pnorm(0.448/(1.35*sqrt(2/n)) - 1.96) = 0.718 (n=117), 0.763 (n=130); power.t.test(n=130, delta=0.448, sd=1.35) = 0.760. Same pattern for the primary: SD 25.5, 117/group gives 85% not 90%. Cannot determine which input is wrong; K indeterminate.

rows.R: eTable 4 (supp3 p6) glucose 12 wk: arm changes 0.09 (-0.07 to 0.24) and 0.15 (-0.01 to 0.31), contrast 0.07 (-1.19 to 1.33); the contrast interval is about 5-6 times wider than the arm intervals imply (root-sum-square half-width about 0.22) and equals the hsCRP 12-wk tuple. WOMAC total pain 24 wk contrast (-24 to 31) is narrower than the arm CIs imply (about +/-33), unlike earlier WOMAC time points.
rows.evidence: Supp3 p5-6 eTable 4; main p6 Table 2 (text).
rows.rationale: sqrt(0.155^2 + 0.16^2) = 0.223 vs printed half-width 1.26 for glucose 12: clearly a copied interval (see C008). For WOMAC 24, shared random effects could make the contrast narrower than root-sum-square, so that occurrence alone would be indeterminate. Exploratory secondary outcomes; minor.

rows.R: eTable 5 (supp3 p8) WORMS effusion change: krill 10 (12%) of 107 and placebo 16 (12%) of 109; 10/107 = 9.3%, 16/109 = 14.7%.
